name: Mistakes to Avoid When Redesigning Your Kitchen Layout

step.name: Step 1: [ ] Verify measurements repeatedly — Grab a tape measure and double…
step.text: [ ] Verify measurements repeatedly — Grab a tape measure and double-check every dimension, then have your contractor confirm. This ensures cabinets and appliances fit perfectly without last-minute surprises.

step.name: Step 2: [ ] Plan for layered lighting and strong ventilation — Don't just r…
step.text: [ ] Plan for layered lighting and strong ventilation — Don't just rely on a single overhead light. Include task lighting, under-cabinet lighting, and a range hood that’s powerful enough for your cooking style. This prevents dim corners and lingering odors.

step.name: Step 3: [ ] Define clear zones for your work triangle — Focus on the relati…
step.text: [ ] Define clear zones for your work triangle — Focus on the relationship between your refrigerator, sink, and cooktop. Each leg should be generally 4–9 feet, with a combined distance of no more than 26 feet, ensuring efficient movement without unnecessary steps.

step.name: Step 4: [ ] Walk through your planned layout mentally — Imagine yourself co…
step.text: [ ] Walk through your planned layout mentally — Imagine yourself cooking, cleaning, and entertaining in the new space. Does it feel intuitive? Will multiple people be able to use it simultaneously without bumping into each other? This helps balance form and function.

step.name: Step 5: [ ] Finalize all selections before demolition — Avoid changes once…
step.text: [ ] Finalize all selections before demolition — Avoid changes once construction starts. Cabinet lead times can be 6–10 weeks, and countertop templating adds another 2–3 weeks. Having everything decided upfront keeps the project on schedule and within budget.
